clue.text: Fall back in common mutual defence

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the run of letters from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the join

explanation.surface: Allies fall back on a shared pact for defending one another.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'commoN MUTUAl' backwards and the season appears; 'back' signals the reversal and 'in' the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: A sapper colonel donning a vestment — that's fishy !

indicators.note: donning means the following pieces wear the vestment, which sits on top in a down answer

parts.note: an alb is a white priestly vestment
CO is a commanding officer, here a colonel
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers

explanation.surface: An army engineer officer dressed in church robes is suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer what is 'donned' sits on top, so the vestment comes first. A sapper is a soldier of the British army's engineers; 'fishy' is not 'suspicious' but 'that is a fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a species of tuna, so it is a fish.

clue.text: About a pound tip Edward gets — for sloth ?

indicators.note: About means the word for a tip goes round the next pieces

parts.note: a tip is a hint or point
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward receives a pound as a tip for being lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' is the animal, not laziness: its feet are twisted inwards, as a club foot is.
explanation.definitionFit: Taliped means club-footed, and a sloth's turned-in feet are given as an instance.

clue.text: Doctor headed the circle last Sunday

indicators.note: headed means the doctor piece goes at the head of the down answer

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A physician led the group gathered round.
explanation.walkthrough: Mothering Sunday is the British name for Mother's Day, in mid-Lent; the clue was printed the week after.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth Sunday of Lent is called Mothering Sunday in Britain, and that was the previous week's Sunday.

clue.text: Jack Goodman has a trick that's profound

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST
a ruse is a trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: A man called Jack Goodman pulls off a clever, deep trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack Goodman' reads as one person's name but splits into a sailor and a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abstruse is hard to understand, deep in thought, as is a profound idea.

clue.text: Had a cue to go Snark hunting?

definitions.text: Had a cue to go Snark hunting?

parts.words: Had a cue to go Snark hunting
parts.note: Lewis Carroll's Snark crew included a man who scored at a billiard table, and such men carry cues

explanation.walkthrough: In Carroll's 'The Hunting of the Snark' the crew includes a Billiard-marker; 'cue' is the billiard cue, not a prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiard marker keeps the score at billiards, and one sails on Carroll's Snark hunt.

clue.text: 3's home's deserted in Herts

indicators.note: deserted means the letters of home have left the longer word

parts.note: 3-down's answer, the Sunday clue

explanation.surface: A third party's house stands empty in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to 3-down; take the letters H, O, M, E out of it and what is left is a town. Herts is Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, England.

clue.text: Used for serenading a Hawaiian pussy-cat ?

definitions.text: Used for serenading a Hawaiian pussy-cat

parts.words: Used for serenading a Hawaiian pussy-cat
parts.note: recalls Lear's Owl, who sang to the Pussy-cat to a small guitar, here a Hawaiian one

explanation.walkthrough: In Lear's 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat' the Owl sang 'to a small guitar'; the small Hawaiian guitar fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukulele is a small four-stringed guitar from Hawaii.

clue.text: First mother, then son perhaps ? Exactly

parts.note: Eve is the first mother in Genesis

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word son may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother first, then maybe a son, precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal on the son, not a hedge on the definition; 'Exactly' is the old affirming sense, as in the Bible's 'even so, Lord'.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so can mean precisely or just so, an old way of agreeing exactly.

clue.text: Round Tabler taking a drink is booked

parts.note: Tristram was a knight of the Round Table
shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.surface: A knight from Arthur's table has a drink and is reserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' means made into a book: the result is Sterne's novel. Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is the title of Laurence Sterne's comic novel, so the name is in a book.

clue.text: Like East Side-West Side air ballet perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of air ballet may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A dance number set in New York, with East Side and West Side gangs, like West Side Story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns AIR BALLET into an anagram; East Side-West Side has two sides, the sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral means having or involving two sides, as a city split into East and West Sides does.

clue.text: Accustom one to a sequence back East

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: back says the word for a sequence is written right to left

parts.note: a run is a sequence, as of cards or wins
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Getting someone used to a series of events back in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed printed '8' for 'a'; the page reads 'to a sequence'. 'back' turns RUN into NUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to harden or habituate someone to something unpleasant, so it means accustom.

clue.text: Tree Island roughly speaking ?

indicators.note: roughly speaking says the island's name only approximately sounds like the answer

parts.note: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: A tree on an island, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of the island Cyprus, said loosely, sounds like the name of the tree; 'roughly speaking' admits the match is approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is an evergreen conifer often planted in Mediterranean landscapes.

clue.text: Artist's entrance

explanation.surface: The doorway belonging to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingres was a French painter, so 'Artist's' can read as INGRES'S, which sounds and spells like the word for a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingres's is the possessive of the painter Ingres; an ingress is an act or place of going in, an entrance.

clue.text: They have a central meeting place

definitions.text: They have a central meeting place

parts.words: They have a central meeting place
parts.note: lines drawn out from the middle of a circle all meet at its centre

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a club or committee; the 'they' are lines in a circle meeting at its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are straight lines from the centre of a circle to its edge, so all of them meet at the centre.

clue.text: Like the air into which Yetis vanish?

definitions.text: Like the air into which Yetis vanish?

parts.words: Like the air into which Yetis vanish
parts.note: the thin air of high mountains, where elusive snowmen are seldom seen and so are rare

explanation.walkthrough: The air high in the Himalayas is thin; Yetis are rare creatures, so the air they vanish into is made rare, rare-fied.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied air is thin, with low density, as at high altitude.

clue.text: Continent's lost a bishop's office' of course

indicators.note: lost means the continent's name drops the letter given by a

parts.note: Africa is a continent
a see is the seat or office of a bishop

explanation.surface: Africa has naturally lost one bishop's administrative office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' is not 'naturally' but 'belonging to a course of a meal'. 'lost' removes the first A from AFRICA'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a stewed meat dish served as a course in a meal.

clue.text: Laws allow second French person to enter States

indicators.note: to enter means the French pronoun goes into the word States

parts.note: tu is the French second-person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Laws permit a second Frenchman to come into America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second French person' is grammatical: the pronoun for 'you' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written laws passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Source of parchment for high class magazine with backing in hair-styling

indicators.note: in places the reversed pieces inside the hairdo word

parts.note: a perm is a permanent wave, a hair-styling

indicators.note: with backing tells the solver to reverse the class letter and the magazine word together

parts.note: U stands for upper class

explanation.surface: Where an upmarket magazine got its paper, with support from a hairdressing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with backing' turns U + MAG into GAMU, which goes 'in' PERM. Pergamum was the ancient Greek city in Asia Minor that gave its name to parchment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word parchment derives from the city of Pergamum, famed for writing material made from skins.

clue.text: Involve me making return on railway fuel

indicators.note: making return says the word me is turned back to front

parts.note: BR is British Rail, a railway
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Drag me into a railway coming back for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making return' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict, so to involve them.

clue.text: It holds the unloved emperor motionless

indicators.note: holds means the word It wraps round the shortened emperor
unloved means without love, the letter O, which looks like a zero score in tennis

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: Something keeps the hated emperor still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unloved' removes O (love, a zero score) from NERO, leaving NER, which IT 'holds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means having no power to move, so it is still and motionless.

clue.text: "Serenely full, the would say, Fate cannot harm me " (S. Smith)

definitions.text: "Serenely full, the would say, Fate cannot harm me " (S. Smith)

parts.words: "Serenely full, the would say, Fate cannot harm me " (S. Smith)
parts.note: a quotation from Sydney Smith's recipe for salad, with the diner's name blanked out

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash for the missing word. Sydney Smith's verse recipe for salad ends 'Serenely full, the epicure would say, Fate cannot harm me, I have dined today'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet who delights in fine food is the speaker of the line after a good dinner.

clue.text: Taken by bather possibly as he dives in

definitions.text: Taken by bather possibly as he dives in

indicators.note: possibly hints that the word bather may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer gulps air as he plunges in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes BATHER an anagram; the whole clue also describes the gulp of air a diver takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer inhales a lungful of air before plunging under the water.

clue.text: Eight times experienced by a cat ?

definitions.text: Eight times experienced by a cat

parts.words: Eight times experienced by a cat
parts.note: a cat is said to have nine lives, so it starts life over eight times after the first

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb gives a cat nine lives: after the first, it is born again eight times.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth is being born again, which a cat with nine lives does eight times.

clue.text: Annoyed, being one pound in debt

indicators.note: in places the numeral and the pound sign inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
one is the Roman numeral I
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone vexed at owing a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Debts were once written in red ink, so RED is debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means irritated or angered.

clue.text: His feet on the ground — a Spanish royalist ?

indicators.note: Spanish says to put the royal part of the word into Spanish, where royal is real

parts.note: a royalist is a supporter of the monarchy

explanation.surface: A man with his feet planted firmly, who supports the Spanish crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed added a stray quote mark after 'His'. Spanish for royal is REAL, so a royal-ist in Spanish is a REAL-IST. The definition reads 'one whose feet are on the ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a practical, down-to-earth person who sees things as they are.

clue.text: Bikini-a tax

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax, as on a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A levy on swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is not the swimsuit but the Pacific coral island used for nuclear tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a ring-shaped coral island in the Marshall Islands, an example of that kind of reef.

clue.text: Diabolical driving — can't' help it

parts.note: points to the proverb about doing what one must when the devil drives

explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'needs must when the devil drives', meaning necessity compels. 'Diabolical driving' is the devil at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means that when compelled by circumstance one has no choice but to act.

clue.text: Say Christmas decoration time ? There are others

indicators.note: Say signals that the pieces are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: holly is a traditional Christmas decoration; days can mean time, as in 'in my days'

explanation.surface: Is Christmas the time for decorating? Other festive seasons exist too.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed printed a stray quote mark after 'Say'. Christmas is one holiday season among others; HOLLY DAYS spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is one of several breaks from work, such as Easter and summer, in a year.

clue.text: O those exams !

parts.note: a sigh about school tests, which also reads as O followed by the word for those tests

explanation.walkthrough: O levels were the British school exams taken at about sixteen until 1988; the clue's O is the first half of their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Levels completes O-levels, the old British exams, which are grades or stages of attainment.
